propositions: Prompt cache prefix varies per pass within a single plan-review run because each pass has a pass-specific stance suffix after the shared plan-bearing prefix, causing three different cache keys and zero cross-pass reads despite shared leading bytes

Cache breakpoint placement after the pass-specific stance suffix (at the END of the whole system prompt on single-turn calls) sits after the byte-identical shared_plan_prefix boundary, making the shared prefix invisible to content-addressed caching

Plan-review passes write cache on every call at premium rate and never read it within a run, paying a write premium with zero benefit because the cache breakpoint does not align with the shared-prefix boundary

The cache_prefix runner-seam knob moves the breakpoint to the end of byte-stable shared_plan_prefix by sending the prefix as static system_prompt and the pass-specific suffix as a dynamic instruction, enabling cross-pass reads within one run

Same-ticket re-reviews inside the TTL have a byte-stable marked prefix and should read the cache, but this path rarely fires in practice because gate sequences do not typically re-review unchanged tickets within five minutes
